summary: SpaceM is a professional-grade web simulation platform built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge "Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" challenge. Designed for students and aspiring engineers, it transforms complex spaceflight theory into active, interactive systems engineering tasks. The platform features four core modules: an orbital mechanics 3D docking simulator using Three.js, an ISS Environmental Control and Life Support (ECLSS) power management lab for solar storms, an EVA spacesuit and airlock depressurization checklist, and a NASA Human Research Program (HRP) aerospace medicine clinic. By running entirely client-side without heavy software requirements, SpaceM makes authentic mission control training accessible to any classroom worldwide.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

SpaceM is a full-stack, client-side browser simulation suite that trains users in core aerospace engineering and astronaut operations. It features interactive modules including a 3D Orbital Docking simulator (managing RCS thrusters under a 0.2 m/s closing velocity limit), an ECLSS Systems Management lab (allocating power during a Solar Particle Event), and EVA/Aerospace Medicine checklists based on NASA HRP protocols (e.g., depressurizing to 4.3 psi).

2. What benefits does it have and what is the intended impact?

Passive space education loses young learners. SpaceM bridges this gap by turning passive reading into active, hands-on practice. By running entirely in the browser without heavy downloads, it connects classroom science to the real ISS, making authentic mission control training accessible to any classroom worldwide.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, and Software Used:

- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla ES6 JavaScript.

- Graphics & Physics: Three.js (WebGL) for 3D simulation.

- APIs: NASA EONET and WhereTheISS for live telemetry.

- AI Tools: Used for debugging, structuring code logic, and formatting documentation.
